rules.rule: Urgent: eye/vision symptoms with danger signs
rules.problem: Acute glaucoma, gonococcal, orbital cellulitis, stroke and jaundice branches depend on diagnoses from rules above (stroke lacks TIA; glaucoma rule too strict), so those danger signs may not fire. Priority itself is justified by the red box heading. Chemical burn lacks eye site. Preeclampsia/postpartum branch uses onset <= 1 week, consistent with briefing convention.

summary: Acute glaucoma diagnosis requires every listed feature (pain, red eye, blurred vision, haloes, fixed pupil plus headache/nausea/vomiting), likely much stricter than the page and rarely firing. The stroke diagnosis omits TIA, the STI and chemical burn concepts are looser than the page, and the single-eye allergic/localised-cause branch and pre-eclampsia diagnosis are not encoded. Most urgent triggers and the probable/likely diagnoses are otherwise faithful.
